mainTopic: בושת and פגם in אונס, who receives them and how פגם is measured, and the משנה on מכר and קנס by age
overview: The amud opens by finishing the search for a source that the attacker in an אונס case pays בושת and פגם on top of the fixed fifty-סלע קנס. אביי rejects רבי זירא's logical proofs by comparing to the fixed thirty for a slave, and then אביי and רבא each prove it from the פסוק. The גמרא asks why these payments go to the father and not the girl. It tries the פסוק 'בנעוריה בית אביה', limits it to vows, rejects learning from איסור or from קנס, and settles on logic: the father controls whom she marries. Next, the גמרא explains how פגם is measured: by the price gap between a virgin and a non-virgin maidservant bought as a wife for a slave the master is pleased with. A new משנה then teaches that sale and קנס never apply to the same girl: a קטנה can be sold, a נערה gets a קנס, and a בוגרת has neither. רב says this is only רבי מאיר's view, and a ברייתא shows that חכמים give a קנס even to a קטנה from three years and a day. Each side's source is explained, and the amud ends with a discussion of ריש לקיש's teaching about the full and short spellings of 'נערה'.

steps.title: Even a slave who does simple needlework is worth thirty
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his rejection of רבי זירא's first proof: the Torah's thirty for a slave is fixed, whether the slave is highly skilled or only does simple sewing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a slave who only does needlework also get thirty?!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of אביי's rejection that began before this section. He points out that the Torah gives thirty סלעים for any slave killed by an ox, even a slave with only a simple skill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא had argued that the fifty for אונס cannot be the whole payment, because then a daughter of high standing and a commoner's daughter would get the same. אביי answers that the Torah does exactly that with slaves: a fixed sum no matter the victim's value. So a fixed fifty is not strange, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: needlework, a simple and low-paid skill
thirty (סלעים), the fixed payment for a slave killed by an ox
a slave

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new argument. It closes a challenge that started before this section, so read it together with אביי's earlier words about a skilled slave.

phrases.english: one who does needlework — thirty?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rejection of רבי זירא's first proof, which came before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זירא's first proof, which compared a כהן גדול's daughter to a commoner's daughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah does set fixed sums no matter how valuable the victim is, as with a slave. So an equal fifty for every girl proves nothing.

steps.title: רבי זירא's second proof: two attackers
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that if one man violated a girl in an unnatural way and a second man then violated her normally, it would make no sense for both to pay the same fifty. So there must be extra payments that change from case to case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: If two men forced themselves on her, one in the normal way and one in an unnatural way, people will say: one who violated an untouched girl pays fifty, and one who violated a damaged girl also pays fifty?
steps.whatsHappening: After his first proof was rejected, רבי זירא tries a new one. He describes a girl attacked by two men and asks how both could pay exactly the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl violated in an unnatural way still counts as a בתולה for the קנס, so a second attacker also owes fifty. But she has already been harmed, so her shame and lost value are smaller. If fifty were the whole payment, both would pay equally, which seems wrong. That suggests fifty is a fixed קנס, with extra amounts added according to the harm.

keyTerms.meaning: in the normal way
in an unnatural way
whole, untouched
damaged, already harmed
had relations with

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
If two men had forced themselves on her,
one in the normal way, and one in an unnatural way,
people will say: one who violated an untouched girl pays fifty,
and one who violated a damaged girl also pays fifty?
phrases.notes: He means the second man, who came after she was already harmed in the unnatural way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first proof is rejected, רבי זירא offers a new logical proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the fifty is only a fixed קנס, with בושת and פגם paid on top.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that an untouched girl and an already-harmed girl should not be valued the same.

steps.title: אביי: the same is true of a healthy slave and a sick slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the new proof with his slave comparison again: a healthy slave and a slave covered in boils both get thirty, so a fixed sum for victims of different value is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, then with a slave too people will say: a healthy slave is thirty, and a slave with boils is also thirty?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's second proof the same way he answered the first. The Torah gives a fixed thirty even when one slave is worth much more than another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's argument depends on the idea that the Torah would not set one price for victims of different worth. אביי shows that with slaves it does exactly that. So the two-attackers case also does not prove that fifty is only part of the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
healthy
covered in boils, very sick

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד נָמֵי, יֹאמְרוּ:
phrases.english: If so, regarding a slave too, people will say:
a healthy slave — thirty,
a slave covered in boils — also thirty?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's second proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רבי זירא's two-attackers proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah does set fixed sums for victims of different worth, as with slaves, so an equal fifty is not a problem.

steps.title: אביי's proof from 'because he tormented her'
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a proof from the פסוק: the fifty is paid 'because he tormented her,' so it covers only the suffering. That means בושת and פגם are separate payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The פסוק says 'because he tormented her.' These fifty are for 'because he tormented her,' which shows that there is also בושת and פגם.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic did not work, אביי turns to the wording of the Torah. He reads the reason the פסוק gives for the fifty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the fifty to the suffering the girl went through. If the fifty is for the suffering, then her shame and her lost value are not included in it. So they must be paid in addition.

keyTerms.meaning: because he tormented her
this shows that there is also
payment for shame
payment for lost value

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: The verse says:
"because he tormented her"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

phrases.english: these fifty are for "because he tormented her,"
which shows that there is also shame and lost value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר קְרָא: תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִינָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logical proofs with a proof from the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That בושת and פגם are paid on top of the fifty.

steps.title: רבא's proof from 'the man who lay with her'
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads a different part of the same פסוק: the fifty is paid by 'the man who lay with her,' so it is for the pleasure of the act. That means בושת and פגם are separate payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'And the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty silver.' Fifty is for the pleasure of lying with her, which shows that there is also בושת and פגם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own proof from the same פסוק, but from different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא focuses on the phrase 'the man who lay with her' and understands the fifty as payment for the pleasure he took. Like אביי, he concludes that because the fifty has one specific purpose, shame and lost value must be paid separately. The two proofs reach the same result through different words.

keyTerms.meaning: who lay with her
the pleasure of lying with her
the girl's father

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"And the man who lay with her shall give
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

phrases.english: to the father of the young woman fifty silver."
For the pleasure of lying with her — fifty,
which shows that there is also shame and lost value.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא: וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשּׁוֹכֵב עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק that reaches the same result as אביי.
steps.raayaObject: That בושת and פגם are paid on top of the fifty.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא agree that the fifty is a fixed קנס and that בושת and פגם are added. They only disagree about which words of the פסוק prove it.

steps.title: Maybe the extra payments go to the girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק only says the fifty goes to the father. Maybe the extra payments of בושת and פגם go to the girl herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say they go to her?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know there are extra payments, the גמרא asks who gets them. Since the shame and harm are hers, maybe she should receive them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the father only for the fifty. The extra payments come from a הלכה we learned through inference, so the פסוק never said who receives them. The challenge is that they might belong to the girl.

keyTerms.meaning: but maybe say
to her, to the girl herself

phrases.english: But maybe say these go to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the extra payments proven by אביי and רבא and asks who receives them.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that בושת and פגם go to the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק gives only the fifty to the father. The extra payments are for her own shame and harm, so maybe they belong to her.

steps.title: All the gains of a young girl go to her father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from a פסוק: 'in her youth, in her father's house.' This teaches that every gain connected to a girl's youth belongs to her father, including בושת and פגם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'in her youth, in her father's house,' so all the gains of her youth go to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a general rule from the Torah about a נערה and her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is broad: any gain that comes from a girl during her years as a נערה goes to her father. Payments for her shame and lost value fall under that rule. So they go to the father just like the fifty.

keyTerms.meaning: in her youth, in her father's house
gain, profit
her youth, her years as a נערה

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא gives בושת and פגם to the father from 'בנעוריה בית אביה'. Steps 8–9 knock down this source, and Step 12 gives the final reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer seems to settle who gets the extra payments, but Steps 8–9 show that this פסוק is only about הפרת נדרים, not money.

phrases.english: The verse says: "in her youth, in her father's house,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:17

phrases.english: all the gains of her youth go to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about who receives the extra payments.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that teaches a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra payments for her shame and harm might belong to the girl herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: All gains of a נערה belong to her father, so בושת and פגם go to him.

steps.title: If the youth פסוק covers everything, why did רב need the maidservant פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 7. רב derived that a daughter's handiwork belongs to her father from the comparison to a maidservant. If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' already gives the father every gain, that derivation would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רב הונא's teaching in the name of רב? He asked how we know a daughter's handiwork belongs to her father, and answered from the פסוק comparing her to a maidservant. Why would he need that? He could have learned it from 'in her youth, in her father's house'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 7 by pointing to another teaching that seems to ignore that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' really taught that all of a girl's gains go to her father, it would also cover her handiwork. רב's roundabout proof from אמה shows that he did not read that פסוק so broadly. So Step 7's source now looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Her handiwork, meaning what she earns from her work
A Jewish maidservant
Let him derive it from a different, simpler source
Why do I need this?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But then, that which רב הונא said in the name of רב:
From where do we know that a daughter's handiwork belongs to her father?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכּוֹר אִישׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה.
phrases.english: As it says: 'And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7

phrases.english: Just as a maidservant's handiwork goes to her master,
so too a daughter's handiwork goes to her father.
Why do I need this?
Let him learn it from 'in her youth, in her father's house'!
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק the גמרא used in Step 7 to say every gain of her youth goes to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בנעוריה בית אביה' as covering all of a girl's gains
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that פסוק covers everything, רב's separate proof for handiwork would be unnecessary.

steps.title: The youth פסוק is only about canceling vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'בנעוריה בית אביה' is written about a father canceling his daughter's vows, not about money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that פסוק is written about canceling vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by limiting the youth פסוק to הפרת נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רב needed the אמה proof for handiwork. But it also takes away the source Step 7 used for giving בושת and פגם to the father, so the גמרא now needs a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A father's or husband's canceling of a girl's vows

steps.confusionAlert: This answer saves רב's teaching, but it knocks down the answer from Step 7. The question of who gets בושת and פגם is open again until Step 12 answers it with logic.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הַהִיא בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב.
phrases.english: Rather, that פסוק is written about canceling vows.
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:17

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הַהִיא בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by narrowing the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The youth פסוק gives the father every gain of his daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The youth פסוק only gives the father the power to cancel her vows.

steps.title: We cannot learn money laws from ritual laws
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest extending the father's control over vows to money matters. The גמרא rejects this: money law is not learned from איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn money matters from the vows case. We do not learn money law from ritual law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks one possible way to rescue the father's right to בושת and פגם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows belong to איסור, meaning what is forbidden or permitted, while בושת and פגם are ממון. The rule is that a law in one area cannot be copied into the other. So the father's authority over vows does not prove he gets the money.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject
We do not learn money laws from ritual (forbidden/permitted) laws

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn from it,
phrases.notes: From it means from the vows case: since the father controls her vows, maybe he controls her money too.

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from ritual matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects one attempt to restore the father's right after Step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed comparison from vows to money
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Ritual law and money law are separate areas and cannot be compared.

steps.title: We cannot learn money laws from a fine
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest learning from the fifty-shekel קנס, which the Torah gives to the father. The גמרא rejects this: ordinary money law is not learned from קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn from the fine. We do not learn money law from a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second way of proving that the father gets בושת and פגם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says outright that the fifty-shekel קנס goes to the father. But a קנס is a special penalty beyond normal payment, so ordinary payments like בושת and פגם cannot be modeled on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine: a fixed penalty set by the Torah, not ordinary compensation
We do not learn ordinary money laws from fines

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn from the fine,
phrases.notes: He means the fifty silver pieces, which the פסוק itself says go to the father.

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a second attempt, parallel to Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed comparison from the fine to בושת and פגם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קנס is a special penalty and cannot serve as a model for regular payments.

steps.title: Logic: the father gets the payments because he controls her marriage
steps.stepSummary: With no פסוק left, the גמרא concludes from reasoning that בושת and פגם belong to the father. He could marry her off to a repulsive man or one covered in boils, so her shame is under his control.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it makes sense that the payment belongs to her father, since if he wanted, he could hand her over in marriage to a repulsive man or a man covered with boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to Step 6's question: the father gets בושת and פגם because of plain logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she is a נערה, the father has the legal power to marry her to someone who would shame and lower her. Since her shame and loss of value are in his hands, the payment for them belongs to him too.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense: a conclusion from reasoning, not from a פסוק
A repulsive, disgusting man
A man covered with boils

steps.whatToRemember: בושת and פגם go to the father not because of a פסוק, but because of logic: he controls whom she marries, so he could have shamed her himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles the question from Step 6 that the payments beyond the fifty go to the father, not to the girl.

phrases.english: Rather, it makes sense that it belongs to her father,
since if he wanted, he could hand her over in marriage
to a repulsive man or a man covered with boils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected sources with a reason from logic
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The father receives בושת and פגם because he has the power to marry her off, even to someone who would shame her.

steps.title: The משנה: measure פגם as if she were a maidservant being sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: פגם is measured by viewing her as a maidservant for sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: For פגם, we view her as if she were a maidservant being sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes the משנה's rule for measuring פגם, setting up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We imagine her on the slave market and compare her price before the act with her price after it. The difference is the פגם payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Loss of value: the drop in her worth caused by the act
A maidservant being sold on the market

phrases.english: For loss of value, we view her
as if she were a maidservant being sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּגָם, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִילּוּ הִיא שִׁפְחָה נִמְכֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: how to measure פגם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פגם is measured by her value as a maidservant on the market.

steps.title: How exactly do we estimate her value?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this estimate is actually done.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we estimate her value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical method of estimating פגם, and the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the general idea but not the method. The גמרא wants to know exactly which two prices are being compared.

keyTerms.meaning: We estimate the price

phrases.english: How do we estimate her value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the משנה's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of estimating פגם

steps.title: אבוה דשמואל: compare a virgin and non-virgin maidservant bought for service
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל says we estimate the difference a person would pay for a virgin maidservant versus a non-virgin maidservant to serve him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבוה דשמואל said: We estimate how much a person would be willing to pay for a virgin maidservant compared with a non-virgin maidservant, to serve him.
steps.whatsHappening: אבוה דשמואל answers with a method: compare the prices of two maidservants who differ only in being a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The price gap between the two maidservants is the פגם. But he speaks of buying her 'to serve him', which the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: We estimate
A virgin / a non-virgin

phrases.english: שמואל's father said:
We estimate how much a person would be willing to pay
for a virgin maidservant
compared with a non-virgin maidservant, to serve him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The price difference between a virgin and a non-virgin maidservant bought to serve

steps.title: For serving him, what difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if he buys her only to work, whether she is a virgin should not change her price.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבוה דשמואל's method, because for housework her being a virgin does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both maidservants would work equally well, a buyer would pay the same for both. Then the method would show no price gap, and the פגם would come out as zero.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: What difference does it make to him?
phrases.notes: Someone buying her just to serve him: why would her being a virgin matter to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'to serve him' in אבוה דשמואל's method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For service alone, her being a virgin does not affect her price, so there is nothing to measure.

steps.title: Rather: the buyer wants her as a wife for his slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises the method: compare a non-virgin and a virgin maidservant bought to marry to his slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the comparison is between a maidservant who had relations and one who did not, for marrying her to his slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the method by changing why the maidservant is being bought: as a wife for the master's slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a virgin matters for a wife, so now there can be a real price gap. That gap is the פגם.

keyTerms.meaning: To marry her to his slave

phrases.english: Rather, between a maidservant who had relations
and a maidservant who did not have relations,
for marrying her to his slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּין שִׁפְחָה בְּעוּלָה לְשִׁפְחָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּעוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by changing the purpose of the purchase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She is bought to serve the master.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is bought to be married to the master's slave.

steps.title: Why would the master care what wife his slave gets?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: a master would not pay more just so his slave gets a virgin wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for his slave, what difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the revised method, because a master usually does not care about his slave's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A master normally would not spend extra money on his slave's happiness. Without a reason to pay more for a virgin, there is still no price gap to measure.

phrases.english: And for his slave, what difference does it make to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the revised method in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: Marrying her to his slave as the basis for the estimate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A master has no reason to pay more for his slave's wife, so there is still no price gap.

steps.title: A slave the master is pleased with
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we picture a slave who gives his master satisfaction, so the master is happy to pay more to reward him with a virgin wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a slave whose master is pleased with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the method by describing a master who has a reason to pay extra for his slave's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A master who is pleased with his slave wants to reward him, so he would pay more for a virgin. The extra amount he would pay is the פגם that the offender must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Satisfaction, pleasure

steps.whatToRemember: פגם is measured by how much more a master would pay for a virgin maidservant than for a non-virgin one, as a wife for a slave he is pleased with.

phrases.english: It is talking about a slave whose master has
satisfaction from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֶבֶד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְרַבּוֹ קוֹרַת רוּחַ הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 and completes the method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No master would pay extra for his slave's wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: A master who is pleased with his slave would pay extra, and that difference is the פגם.

steps.title: New משנה: sale and fine never go together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a father's right to sell his daughter and a rapist's fine never apply to the same girl. A קטנה can be sold but gets no fine. A נערה gets a fine but cannot be sold. A בוגרת gets neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever there is sale, there is no fine. Wherever there is a fine, there is no sale. A minor can be sold and has no fine. A young woman has a fine and cannot be sold. A grown woman has neither.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a simple rule: sale and fine never apply to the same girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the girl's age stage. A father can sell only a קטנה as a maidservant. The fine for rape goes only to a נערה. A בוגרת is out of her father's control, so neither law applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Sale: a father selling his young daughter as a Hebrew maidservant
A fixed fine (fifty סלעים) paid by a rapist or seducer to the girl's father
A minor girl, before she shows signs of puberty
A young woman: from the first signs of puberty for about six months
A fully grown woman, past the נערה stage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three stages. קטנה, then נערה, then בוגרת. Each one has a different set of laws.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Any place where there is sale —
phrases.notes: This means a father selling his young daughter as a maidservant.

phrases.english: there is no fine.
And any place where there is a fine —
there is no sale.
A minor — she can be sold,
and she has no fine.
A young woman — she has a fine,
and she cannot be sold.

phrases.aramaic: הַבּוֹגֶרֶת — אֵין לָהּ לֹא מֶכֶר וְלֹא קְנָס.
phrases.english: A grown woman — she has neither sale nor fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר אֵין קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of how to measure the damage payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sale and fine never apply to the same girl: a קטנה can be sold, a נערה gets a fine, a בוגרת has neither.

steps.title: רב: the משנה follows רבי מאיר only
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה is only רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say a girl can get a fine even at an age when she can also be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But חכמים say she gets a fine even where there is sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us the משנה is not everyone's opinion. It is רבי מאיר's view, and חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חכמים, sale and fine can overlap. A קטנה who can be sold still gets the fine if she is raped. So the משנה's rule 'never together' belongs to רבי מאיר alone.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the opinion of; it marks a ruling as one side of a dispute
The Sages, the majority view
In a place (case) where there is sale

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
but the Sages say:
she has a fine even where there is sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the משנה follows and introduces a dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים hold that a fine applies even to a girl who can be sold.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא showing the dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows both views. רבי מאיר gives the same age split as the משנה. חכמים say any girl from age three and a day until she becomes a בוגרת gets a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A minor, from one day old until she has two hairs, can be sold and has no fine. From two hairs until she matures, she has a fine and cannot be sold. This is רבי מאיר's view, since he said: wherever there is sale there is no fine, and wherever there is a fine there is no sale. חכמים say: a girl from three years and one day until she matures has a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר and חכמים really argue about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's words in the ברייתא match the משנה exactly, so the משנה is his. חכמים start the fine at age three and a day, which is well inside the קטנה stage. That shows they let the fine apply even to a girl who can still be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs: the sign of puberty that makes a girl a נערה
Until she matures into a בוגרת
Three years and one day: the youngest age at which this law applies, according to חכמים

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
A minor, from one day old
until she grows two hairs
phrases.notes: Two hairs are the sign of puberty. Once they appear, she is a נערה.

phrases.aramaic: — יֵשׁ לָהּ מֶכֶר וְאֵין לָהּ קְנָס.
phrases.english: — she can be sold and has no fine.
From when she grows two hairs until she matures

phrases.aramaic: — יֵשׁ לָהּ קְנָס וְאֵין לָהּ מֶכֶר,
phrases.english: — she has a fine and cannot be sold;
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֶכֶר — אֵין קְנָס,
phrases.english: Any place where there is sale — there is no fine,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קְנָס — אֵין מֶכֶר.
phrases.english: and any place where there is a fine — there is no sale.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A minor from three years and one day old
until she matures — she has a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's claim with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the משנה is רבי מאיר's view alone and that חכמים allow a fine where there is sale.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי מאיר's age split and חכמים's view that the fine applies from age three and a day.

steps.title: Do חכמים deny that a father can sell her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of חכמים: they mention only the fine. Does that mean they hold a father cannot sell his young daughter?
steps.simpleTranslation: A fine, yes, but sale, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in how חכמים are quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים say only 'she has a fine,' as if the fine replaces sale. But the Torah clearly allows a father to sell a קטנה. So their wording cannot mean that sale disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

phrases.english: A fine, yes, but sale, no?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of חכמים in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of חכמים in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning only the fine suggests that sale does not apply, but a father may surely sell his minor daughter.

steps.title: Correct the wording: a fine even where there is sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: חכמים mean that she gets the fine as well as being sellable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: she has a fine even where there is sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting how we read חכמים's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים do not take away the father's right to sell. They add that the fine also applies at that age. This matches רב's version of their view in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way instead); used to fix the wording of a source
Even, also

phrases.english: Say instead:
she has a fine even where there is sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים seemed to say there is a fine instead of sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים hold that both sale and fine apply to a קטנה from age three and a day.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: sale and fine never overlap. חכמים: a קטנה from three years and a day can be sold and also gets a fine.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks for רבי מאיר's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what source רבי מאיר uses to show that a קטנה gets no fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the sources. רב חסדא asks why רבי מאיר holds this, and he answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the dispute is clear, the גמרא wants each side's verse. This line sets up רבי מאיר's source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute itself to the sources behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind רבי מאיר's view that a קטנה gets no fine.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's verse: she must be able to marry herself
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the rapist says 'and to him she shall be as a wife.' That fits only a girl who can marry on her own, which means a נערה, not a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And to him she shall be as a wife.' The verse is talking about a girl who can marry by herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers his own question with the verse רבי מאיר relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine passage ends with the rapist marrying her. רבי מאיר reads this as talking only about a girl able to make herself his wife. That rules out a קטנה, so she gets no fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Can make herself (a wife); able to marry on her own

phrases.english: The verse says: "And to him she shall be as a wife" —
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of one who can make herself a wife.
phrases.notes: He means a girl who can marry on her own. That is a נערה, not a קטנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ולו תהיה לאשה' refers to a girl able to marry herself, which excludes a קטנה from the fine.

steps.title: What is חכמים's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source חכמים use to include a קטנה in the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for חכמים's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים must explain why a קטנה gets the fine, even though the verse says 'נערה.' This line opens that question.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis (חכמים)? A short way of asking for their reason

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי מאיר's source to חכמים's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind חכמים's view that a קטנה gets the fine.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'נער' is written without the ה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that in the fine passage, 'נערה' is written 'נער' without the final ה. That spelling includes even a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The verse says 'נער' (written without the ה), so even a minor is included.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives חכמים's source, which comes from how the word is spelled in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read 'נערה' but written 'נער.' Since the full form is missing, חכמים learn that the law is not limited to a full נערה. A קטנה is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Spelled נער without the ה, but read as נערה
Is included in the meaning

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The verse says: "na'ar",
phrases.notes: In the Torah scroll it is written נער, without the ה at the end, even though we read it נערה.

phrases.english: even a minor is included in its meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר קְרָא נַעֲרָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spelling 'נער' without the ה includes a קטנה in the fine.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר learns from 'ולו תהיה לאשה' that only a girl able to marry herself gets the fine. חכמים learn from the short spelling 'נער' that even a קטנה is included.

steps.title: רב פפא reports the teaching to רב שימי בר אשי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, son of רב חנן from בי כלוחית, heard ריש לקיש's teaching and repeated it to רב שימי בר אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, son of רב חנן from בי כלוחית, heard this and went and said it before רב שימי בר אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the next step. Someone repeats ריש לקיש's teaching to another sage, who reacts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is decided here. The line prepares us for רב שימי's reply, which ties ריש לקיש's teaching to a different subject.

keyTerms.meaning: He heard it
He went and said it before (a teacher)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa heard it,
son of Rav Chanan, from Bei Kelochit,

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל אַמְרַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: and went and said it before Rav Shimi bar Ashi.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמְעַהּ רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנָן מִבֵּי כְלוֹחִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how ריש לקיש's teaching from step 28 was passed on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: ריש לקיש's teaching is brought before רב שימי בר אשי.

steps.title: Another version: ריש לקיש was speaking about מוציא שם רע
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says his school learned ריש לקיש's teaching differently. Where 'נערה' is written in full, as in the מוציא שם רע passage, a קטנה is excluded, so one who slanders a קטנה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You teach it on that topic. We teach it on this topic: ריש לקיש said, one who slanders a minor is exempt, since it says 'and they shall give to the father of the נערה,' and here the verse wrote נערה in full.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי gives a second version of ריש לקיש's teaching. It is about a husband who falsely claims his bride was not a virgin, not about the rape fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מוציא שם רע passage, 'נערה' is spelled in full with the ה, so it means only a real נערה. Someone who slanders a קטנה therefore pays nothing. The same spelling idea works in reverse: where the ה is missing, as in the rape passage, a קטנה would be included.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural) / we; contrasts two schools' traditions
You teach / we teach (a tradition)
One who slanders his bride by falsely claiming she was not a virgin
Full: spelled with all its letters

phrases.english: He said to him:
You teach it on that matter.
We teach it on this matter,
phrases.notes: Same teaching, different place: 'that' is the rape fine, 'this' is מוציא שם רע.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל הַקְּטַנָּה — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: One who slanders a minor — is exempt,
as it is stated: "And they shall give to the father of the young woman,"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:19

phrases.english: the verse spoke of "na'ara" written in full.
phrases.notes: Here the ה is written, so only a real נערה counts, and a קטנה is left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן אַהָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ אֲנַן אַהָא מַתְנֵינַן לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different tradition of where ריש לקיש's spelling teaching was said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slanders a קטנה is exempt, because 'נערה' is written in full in the מוציא שם רע passage.
steps.whatToRemember: The spelling rule works both ways. Full 'נערה' means only a נערה. Short 'נער' includes a קטנה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי does not reject ריש לקיש. He only reports that his school attached ריש לקיש's spelling teaching to מוציא שם רע instead of the rape fine.

steps.title: A minor is excluded anyway, because she cannot be stoned
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks רב שימי בר אשי's version. The מוציא שם רע passage ends with stoning, and a קטנה is not punished, so the full spelling is not needed to exclude her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objects: You are saying the only reason a minor is excluded is that the Torah wrote 'נערה' in full, so otherwise we would have included even a minor? But the verse says that if the claim is true, they take the girl out and stone her. A minor is not subject to punishment!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges the version of ריש לקיש's teaching from step 30. He argues that the full spelling cannot be what excludes a קטנה in the מוציא שם רע case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי בר אשי's version makes the full spelling 'נערה' the source for excluding a קטנה. But that same section speaks of stoning the girl if the slander turns out true, and a קטנה is never punished. She is already excluded from the case by logic, so a spelling hint to exclude her would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it, a sharp challenge
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have thought
Subject to punishment
And they shall stone her

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava strongly objects to this:
The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'נערה' (with a ה),
phrases.notes: He is quoting רב שימי בר אשי's version from step 30, where the full spelling is what leaves out a קטנה.

phrases.english: so if it were not so,
I would have said even a minor girl is included?
But isn't it written:
'And if this matter was true,'
'the signs of virginity were not found for the young woman,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָה אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ
phrases.english: 'then they shall bring the young woman out to the entrance of her father's house'
'and stone her.'
And a minor girl is not subject to punishment!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version of ריש לקיש's teaching that רב שימי בר אשי reported in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's claim that the full spelling 'נערה' in the מוציא שם רע passage is what excludes a קטנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The passage ends with stoning, and a קטנה cannot be punished. So she is already excluded, and the spelling cannot be the reason for excluding her.

steps.title: The full spelling here is a model for the short spelling elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates the teaching. Here, in מוציא שם רע, 'נערה' is written in full. This teaches that wherever 'נער' is written without the ה, even a קטנה is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the teaching should be put this way: here the word is written 'נערה' in full. From this we learn that wherever the Torah writes 'נער' without the ה, even a minor girl is meant.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge, the גמרא gives the correct version of ריש לקיש's teaching. The full spelling here is a contrast case. It shows what the short spelling means in other places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה is already excluded from מוציא שם רע by the stoning verse, so the full spelling there is not needed to exclude her. Instead, it serves as a model: when the Torah means only a true נערה, it writes the ה. So wherever the ה is missing, as in the קנס passage, a קטנה is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a corrected version
Every place, wherever
The word written without the final ה
Included in the meaning

steps.whatToRemember: Full spelling 'נערה' means only a true נערה. Short spelling 'נער' includes even a קטנה. This is why חכמים say the קנס applies to a קטנה too.

phrases.english: Rather: here it says 'נערה' (written in full),
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the מוציא שם רע passage, where a קטנה is already left out because she cannot be stoned.

phrases.english: which teaches that every place where it says 'נער' (without the ה),
even a minor girl is included in the meaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge by rewording ריש לקיש's teaching so the spelling serves a real purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the teaching: the full spelling becomes a model case instead of an exclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The full spelling 'נערה' in מוציא שם רע is what excludes a קטנה from that law.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קטנה is excluded there by the stoning verse. The full spelling teaches that the short spelling 'נער' elsewhere includes a קטנה.
